title: I Love Liberty Sticker

description.main: Die-cut vinyl sticker reproducing Roy Lichtenstein's I Love Liberty (1982), made by the Brooklyn studio Apply under license from the artist's estate and sold by the Whitney Museum shop.
description.extended:
A die-cut vinyl sticker reproducing Roy Lichtenstein's I Love Liberty (1982), his Statue of Liberty image, produced by the Brooklyn studio Apply and sold by the Whitney Museum shop.

Screen-printed on premium vinyl and die-cut to the image, the sticker measures 2 by 3 inches. It shows the head and raised torch of the statue in yellow and black against diagonal blue hatching. Lichtenstein made the image as a poster and print for the I Love Liberty television celebration of 1982. Apply produced the sticker under license from the Estate of Roy Lichtenstein as one of four Lichtenstein images. The Whitney stocked the set in 2026 ahead of its retrospective Roy Lichtenstein: Like New (October 11, 2026 to May 10, 2027).

Lichtenstein (1923-1997) arrived at his signature manner in 1961: subjects lifted from comic strips and advertisements, painted in flat colour with hand-drawn Benday dots. By 1964 he was among the most recognised and most contested of the Pop artists. The Whitney holds 460 of his works, including the Roy Lichtenstein Study Collection given by the artist's foundation.

notes: Screen-printed on premium vinyl, dishwasher safe. Copyright line: 2024, Estate of Roy Lichtenstein. Acquired from the Whitney Museum Shop: https://shop.whitney.org/products/lichtenstein-i-love-liberty-sticker
